conflict_topics: disputed saved seat (tissue packet claim) between Agent A and Agent B
who takes the next freed seat (Agent A vs. Agent D)
aisle obstruction / holding of tray-bowl while someone steps away
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers give concise practical reasons (tissue packet, can't carry open bowl); exchanges feel natural for a hawker-centre setting.
Agent D repeats similar waiting statements (Turns 7/9/12 and 21/25), producing some redundancy.
No confusion about physical constraints (fixed stools, no extra chairs); participants reference these constraints implicitly in offers.
evaluation.final_reason: No affirmative settlement occurred. Agent B explicitly refused to give the seat ('No, I can't give you the seat. My tray and bowl are set out...') and Agent A repeatedly requested the seat and offered to hold the tray/bowl, but B never accepted. Agent D agreed to wait after A clarified he would not cut ahead ('No — I won't cut ahead...'; 'Okay — I'll wait'), yet the central A vs. B incompatibility about the occupied seat remained unaddressed by B through the end of the transcript.
position_change_notes: Agent A softened behaviorally (stepped out of the aisle) and made a concrete accommodation offer to enable B to step away, but kept the core claim to the saved seat.
Agent B retained the original position (refusal to give up the seat) and did not change stance in the transcript.
Agent D initially asserted intent to take the next available seat but accepted A's clarification and withdrew active competition (agreed to wait).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A: 'I left that tissue packet here to save this seat. I need to sit and eat; can you give me the seat back?' Turn 2: Agent B: 'No, I can't give you the seat. My tray and bowl are set out and I can't carry the open bowl; come back when I'm finished and I'll move.' Direct, opposing claims to the same seat; unresolved.

Turn 3: Agent A offers a concrete accommodation: 'I'll hold your bowl and tray while you step away briefly...' This is an attempt to resolve the seat dispute. Turn 4: Agent C asks A to step out of the aisle. B's refusal from Round 1 remains unaccepted, so disagreement persists but has softened.

Turn 5: Agent A complies with aisle concern and repeats the offer to hold B's tray/bowl. Turn 6: Agent C asks A to hold the bowl just out of the aisle. No acceptance from B is recorded; substantive dispute between A and B remains but activity shows reduced tension and practical accommodation.

Turn 7: Agent D claims intent to 'take the next seat that frees up.' Turn 8: Agent A: 'I'm sorting this with Agent B now; I'll take the seat when it frees.' The original A-vs-B dispute remains unresolved; a potential A-vs-D timing question appears but A asserts the saved-seat claim.

Turn 9 and Turn 12: Agent D presses whether A will take the seat before D. The core disagreement (A's saved-seat claim vs. B's refusal to give up the seat) continues; D's repeated queries raise mild competition about order but do not resolve the A–B dispute.

Turn 13: Agent A clarifies: 'No — I won't cut ahead. I'm asking Agent B for my saved seat; if it frees now I'll take it, otherwise it's yours.' Turn 14: Agent D: 'Okay — I'll wait.' A–D tension is resolved, but A–B substantive conflict remains (B has not agreed to yield).
No public speech or observable action recorded this round. The unresolved dispute between Agent A (claiming a saved seat) and Agent B (refusing to give it up) persists with no new developments.
Turns 21 & 25: Agent D repeats 'I'll wait' / 'Alright — I'll wait here.' No acceptance from Agent B or a transfer of the seat occurs; the A–B substantive dispute remains unresolved.

substantive_insights: A social cue (a left tissue packet) is used by A to claim a seat, but B does not accept that norm as sufficient to vacate the seat.
A's practical accommodation (offering to hold tray/bowl) would resolve the practical obstacle, but it requires B's acceptance which never occurs.
D's role is secondary; the A–D potential conflict is resolved by A's promise not to cut and D's agreement to wait, leaving the primary unresolved issue between A and B.
